page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g-480s is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top tier. Text processing via Geekbench and text generation for small LLM models also rank in the top tier. Multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation, perform in the average tier. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET, also align with average tier performance. However, prompt processing for medium LLM models represents a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation combined with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated NVMe storage provides a stable resource density for production environments without the performance variability of shared-core instances. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, text processing pipelines, and lightweight database operations.
